compare.intro: To tell this unit's points apart, ask three things: when it happens and whether it happens (〜ます, 〜ません, 〜ました, 〜ませんでした), what job the noun does (を for the thing, へ or に for where you go, に for where something is, で for where you do it or what you use), and whether you are inviting or saying yes (〜ませんか or 〜ましょう).

forms.tag: いる・する · being there or doing there
forms.ja: こうえん{に}[子|こ]どもがいます。こうえん{で}[子|こ]どもがあそびます。
forms.en: There are children in the park. The children play in the park.

forms.tag: どこへ・なにを · where to, or what
forms.ja: [新|あたら]しいきっさてん{へ}[行|い]きます。コーヒー{を}[飲|の]みます。
forms.en: I go to the new café. I drink coffee.

forms.tag: さそう・こたえる · inviting or saying yes
forms.ja: A「[今|いま]から[外|そと]で[食|た]べ{ませんか}。」B「ええ、[食|た]べ{ましょう}。」
forms.en: A: Shall we go and eat out now? B: Yes, let's.

check.label: まちで
check.q: [学校|がっこう]の[前|まえ]（　　）^きっさてんがあります^。
why: で marks where you do something. あります only says where the café is, so the place takes に.
With あります, the place where a thing is takes に: 学校の前に.
を marks the thing an action is done to. あります is not that kind of verb, and the café already has が.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: A「^きのう^、[中川|なかがわ]さんと[山|やま]へ（　　）。」B「はい、^[行|い]きました^。」
why: きのう is past and B answers はい, 行きました, so A asked about the past: 行きましたか.
行きませんか invites someone to go later. You cannot invite someone to yesterday.
行きましょう suggests going later, and B's はい, 行きました does not answer a suggestion.
行きます is not past, so it does not fit きのう, and without か it is not a question.

drill.label: Choose the particle
drill.q: [母|はは]は[月|げつ]よう[日|び]と[木|もく]よう[日|び]に[本|ほん]や（　　）^はたらきます^。
why: へ marks where you go, with verbs like 行きます. はたらきます is something you do at a place.
を marks the thing an action is done to. 本や is where she works, not what she works on.
に goes with verbs like 行きます, 来ます or あります in this unit. はたらきます is an action done there, so it takes で.
The bookshop is where she does the work, so で: 本やではたらきます.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: A「つめたいジュースがありますよ。[飲|の]み（　　）。」B「^ありがとうございます^。いただきます。」
why: A offers a drink: 飲みませんか, "won't you have some?" B thanks A and takes it.
飲みません says "I don't drink". B would not thank A for that.
飲みましたか asks about the past. B's いただきます takes a drink now.
飲みませんでした says "I didn't drink". It is not an offer, so B's thanks do not fit.

drill.label: Choose the phrase
drill.q: A「^きのう^、[何|なに]をしましたか。」B「[友|とも]だちと[駅|えき]の[前|まえ]のデパート（　　）。」
options: でごはんを[食|た]べました
へごはんを[食|た]べました
でごはんを[食|た]べます
にごはんを[食|た]べません
why: The store is where they ate, so で, and きのう needs the past: 食べました.
へ marks where you go. 食べました is done at the store, so the place takes で.
で is right, but 食べます is not past. A asked about きのう.
に does not mark where you eat, and 食べません is neither past nor an answer to "what did you do".

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: A「[金|きん]よう[日|び]の[午後|ごご]、
drill.after: 。」B「いいですね。[会|あ]いましょう。」
drill.hint: Where is the café? Start with the biggest place. The invitation comes last.
drill.full: A「[金|きん]よう[日|び]の[午後|ごご]、[駅|えき]の[中|なか]の{きっさてんで}[会|あ]いませんか。」B「いいですね。[会|あ]いましょう。」
drill.explain: 駅の中の describes the café: the one inside the station. きっさてんで says where you meet, so it takes で, and 会いませんか invites. B says yes with 会いましょう.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: [先週|せんしゅう]の[金|きん]よう[日|び]、うちに
drill.hint: Whose company? Which person? 先週 tells you the time, and the verb comes last.
drill.full: [先週|せんしゅう]の[金|きん]よう[日|び]、うちに[父|ちち]の{[会社|かいしゃ]の}[人|ひと]が[来|き]ました。
drill.explain: 父の会社の人 is someone from father's company. 人が is the one who came, うちに is where they came to, and 先週 needs the past: 来ました.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: きのう　デパートへ　行きましたが、何も　（　　）。
exam.explain: 何も with a negative means "nothing", and きのう needs the past: 何も買いませんでした. 買いました is not negative, so it does not go with 何も. 買いませんか invites and 買いましょう suggests; neither fits a story about yesterday.

exam.label: Choose the particle
exam.q:
A「日よう日、いっしょに　こうえん（　　）　テニスを　しませんか。」
B「ええ、しましょう。」
exam.explain: The park is where you play tennis, so で: こうえんで　テニスを　します. へ marks where you go, with 行きます. を already marks テニス. に would need a verb like 行きます or あります.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.before: A「きのう　ばんごはんは　どこで　食べましたか。」B「
exam.full: A「きのう　ばんごはんは　どこで　食べましたか。」B「友だちの　{うち}で　食べました。」
exam.explain: 友だちの, うち, で, 食べました. 友だちの needs a noun after it, うち. で follows the place where they ate, and the verb comes last in the past, like A's question.

scene.en: The notice board at a language school
scene.intro: Tap each word on the notices pinned to the board in the hallway.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: 日本語の　クラスは　_九時半_に　はじまります。
check.explain: 九時半 is くじはん: nine o'clock is くじ, and 半 is はん. きゅうじ is not used for the time, and 半 does not change to ばん or ぱん after 時.

skill.ask: What time do the students come to school on Friday?
skill.passage:
日本語クラス　今週の　よてい
月よう日〜木よう日
　午前九時〜十二時　クラス（201きょうしつ）
^金よう日^
　^午前は　休みです^。
　^午後一時^〜三時半　中川先生と　えいがを　見ます（305きょうしつ）
土よう日・日よう日　休み
skill.strategy: Find the line for 金よう日 and read only the times under it.

item.q: 学生は　金よう日に　何時に　学校へ　来ますか。
item.explain: Under 金よう日, the morning is 休み, and the film starts at 午後一時. So the students come at one in the afternoon.
why: Nine o'clock is the start time from Monday to Thursday. On Friday the morning is off.
Twelve is when the Monday to Thursday class ends.
Half past three is when the Friday film ends, not when students arrive.
